geometry_notes: There is a 7.4 m S-facing face between W9 b (737.5,443.1) and W10 a (745.0,443.2) that walls.json leaves out. It is the most recognisable face of the building (sv_c6, sv_c7, sv_c10, Teeple photo 013): a two-storey brick block whose upper floor has a cream (precast_cream) box with corner glazing. The box is cantilevered about 2 m out to the S/SE at about 3.3-6.8 m. It has a thin flat roof slab, a silver fascia that tilts up at its outer end, a dark steel drop-rod, and angled glass on its outer face. Under it there is brick with a large ground window (about 2.0 x 1.5 m) at the east end. A narrow brick fin rises past the roof at the box's east edge. It needs its own wall.

A 5 m N-facing jog between W0 b (717.4,472.3) and W1 a (712.5,473.7) is also missing. It is the recessed main-entrance corner, with the brick face carrying 'LYLE S. HALLMAN INSTITUTE FOR HEALTH PROMOTION' (sv_c18, sv_W0).

The west cube is 7.5-8.5 m tall over W3/W4; the rest is 3.6-5 m. Its SE corner overhangs a recessed glazed entrance (W4 s 6.1-9.3) reached by steps from the south path. The cube's own south face sits above the W4-W5 step, and its upper part reads as a plain brick face from the south (sv_W5).

W11 does not face open ground. The lidar shows a slit only 1.5-2.5 m wide outside it (0-3 m nDSM), then the 7 m BMH east block. This is an open-air brick walkway/ramp with a black handrail on a low brick wall (sv_c4, sv_W11_hd55, sv_c16) that runs from the portico plaza SE to the N-S passage. A purple-leaf maple and a tall brick chimney stand in it.

The brick block east of the N-S passage carries the big 'LYLE S. HALLMAN INSTITUTE FOR HEALTH PROMOTION' sign (sv_c7, sv_W10). It reads as part of Teeple's 2003 LHI, but the catalog gives it to BMH's footprint. A glazed level-2 bridge with a brick spandrel and a soffit at about 3 m spans the passage between W10 (s about 0-5) and that block (sv_c6, sv_c10).
Ground falls about 2 m from N (parking, W1) to SE (W8/W9). The roof is level, so W7 goes from 4.9 m at a to 6.8 m at b, and W11 from 6.7 m at a to 4.2 m at b.
